[context_summary]
## Original task
I must write a C program `/app/mystery.c` that performs an operation identical to the pre-compiled binary `/app/mystery`, such that running `./mystery` is behaviorally identical to running `gcc -static -o reversed mystery.c -lm && ./reversed`. Constraints: the C source must be <2KB when gzipped (`cat mystery.c | gzip | wc`), must not invoke `./mystery`, and must be fully self-contained.

## Environment / artifact facts established
- `/app/mystery` is a statically-linked AArch64 (little-endian) ELF executable, no dynamic symbols; `.symtab` intact (glibc + user symbols).
- Running it prints:
  - `Creating high-resolution image: 800x600`
  - `This will be downsampled with ffmpeg after rendering`
  - `Rendering high-resolution image...`
  - `\rProgress: %.1f%%` per row (0.0→100.0)
  - `Rendering complete`, then writes `image.ppm` (P3 ASCII, 800x600, max 255, 5,362,624 bytes), prints `Done.`, exits 0.
- Tools available: gcc, objdump, readelf, strings, nm, od, python3, gzip, wc. No ffmpeg/PIL/file/gdb. CPU is AArch64; `/tmp/t.c` gcc test confirmed `b.mi` / `fcmpe` semantics = branch if operand1 < operand2.
- Image content: blue gradient sky (top ~y<300), red sphere/object center-ish (e.g. pixel (400,300) = (51,10,10)), checkerboard ground plane (gray 152/67 etc.), dark shapes/shadows — a small ray tracer scene.

## Reverse-engineering progress (user functions from nm/objdump)
User symbols (addresses): main (0x400600), vector_create/add/subtract/multiply/dot/length/normalize (0x400cb0–0x400da4), ray_create (0x400db0), ray_at (0x400e10), sphere_intersect (0x400e40), plane_intersect (0x401020), sky_color (0x4010c4
[/context_summary]
